prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] One-file low-poly 3D wallpaper copying the print's composition, palette and subjects, plus a `result.json`.
[action] Read the print via AGY vision (this model cannot see images), wrote `scene/index.html` (Three.js from the allowed CDN, single file, no build), confirmed the page loads with zero console errors and no WebGL failures, wrote `result.json` byte-exact UTF-8, closed the browser tabs/windows opened.
[result] Delivered `./scene/index.html` and `./result.json`. Print = Hokusai-style view, 3 boats, Mount Fuji (富嶽). Scene recreates: huge curling indigo wave left with cream foam crest, smaller foreground wave, three ochre boats with crouched rowers, diagonal swells lower right, distant gray-brown cone with cream snow cap, warm beige sky, cartouche top-left; gentle bob/rock animation. Caveats: I could not see the rendered frame myself (this model cannot view images; screenshots unavailable to me), so the composition is verified by code and a clean page load, not by eyes. fonts/CDN load depends on network.
[next] Open `./scene/index.html` in a browser with network access to Google Fonts and jsdelivr and check the look; the window appears ~1000px; tune camera if needed. No issues found.
